Reusable PSOCK workers for disk-backed fitting

bp_start_psock_pool.Rd

Reuse one group of independent R sessions across streamed dispersion estimation and multiple comparisons, avoiding repeated forks of the parent R session.

Usage

bp_start_psock_pool(matrix_dir, rows = TRUE, cols = TRUE,
                    workers = 1L, verbose = TRUE, timeout = 3600)
bp_stop_psock_pool(pool)
bp_with_psock_pool(pool, code)

Arguments

matrix_dir

Native BPCells matrix directory, readable by every worker.

rows, cols

Row and column indices in analysis order.

workers

Number of independent R sessions.

verbose

Print startup, pass and shutdown diagnostics.

timeout

Socket timeout in seconds.

pool

Pool returned by bp_start_psock_pool.

code

Expression containing fits of pool$counts, using the pool's worker count.

Details

Each worker opens the matrix and selected rows/columns once. Count matrices are not exported as dense data. Register on.exit(bp_stop_psock_pool(pool), add = TRUE) immediately after creating a pool inside a function. A pool belongs to its creating process; scopes cannot be nested. Worker library threads are restricted to one. Numeric workers outside a pool scope retain their existing serial/fork behaviour. A pool does not bypass operating-system process limits. Callbacks referencing other matrices are rejected. The timeout must allow the longest block/pass communication to finish.

Value

The constructor returns a pool environment containing counts. The scope returns the result of code; stopping returns invisible NULL.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
run_comparisons <- function(matrix_dir, design, offset) {
  pool <- bp_start_psock_pool(matrix_dir, workers = 4)
  on.exit(bp_stop_psock_pool(pool), add = TRUE)
  bp_with_psock_pool(pool, {
    dispersion <- bp_estimate_disp_stream(pool$counts, design,
      offset = offset, workers = 4)
    bp_glm_treat(pool$counts, design,
      dispersion = dispersion$tagwise.dispersion, offset = offset, workers = 4)
  })
}
} # }
